correctness.rationale: For finite simple Cartesian tori with 5<=m<=n, any pair whose endpoints differ in both coordinates admits disjoint move-order geodesics, so an edge can be monitored only within its row/column fiber. A cycle subset monitors all edges iff every gap between cyclic consecutive members is strictly shorter than half the circumference. This gives three probes per row/column and lower bound 3n. The placement T={0,floor(m/3),floor(2m/3)} shifted by -floor(mj/n) in column j has column gaps <=ceil(m/3)<m/2. The exact row-block starts J_v=ceil(vn/m) bound row gaps by B=1+ceil((ceil(m/3)-1)n/m)<n/2 for n>=12. Exhaustive elementary inequalities at 5<=m<=n<=11 leave only (5,6) and (7,8), with listed direct row/column certificates. Independent shortest-arc criterion checked on all 8160 cycle subsets of sizes 5..12, and row/column construction checked for 3000 rectangles. These finite checks do not prove the unrestricted theorem; the inequalities and explicit witnesses do.
residual_risks: Publisher papers on circulant and product networks were not fully inspected; this does not affect the direct constructive argument.
